key_insight: AI agents can optimize quantum circuit compilation more reliably when bottleneck subroutines have structure that supports efficient classical verification.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets compilation bottlenecks in Coulomb simulation, Reed–Solomon decoding, and quantum chemistry circuits.
method: Constrain subroutines to reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement-based uncomputation.
Simulate classical inputs and use fuzz testing to check approximate circuit synthesis.
Provide reference implementations and verification constraints to seed a Kaggle optimization competition.
evidence_signal: The abstract discusses three application areas and reference implementations but reports no quantitative compilation improvements or benchmark results.
watch_item: Fuzz-testing certification depends on assumptions about the input distribution and should not be treated as unconditional correctness verification.
paper_title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
